CANON: crucible-residents-v3: the people the board reports on

GROUPS.name: dam and plant staff inside the structure
skeleton crew holding the clean rooms
longshore families in the surge zone
Riverside residents who reach the campus gate

CARDS.name: Tomás Reyes
CARDS.text: First full season. His mother Ines runs the canteen at the Mole and feeds the fleet on credit. He is on the two-man watch when the Harvester breaks her mooring at the peak.

CARDS.name: Priya Nair
CARDS.text: Thirty-six weeks pregnant, scheduled to work the last departure, and on nobody's seat list because she is staff. Her husband is a Heartland lineman stuck at the dam.

CARDS.name: The Albrecht family
CARDS.text: Two parents, two children, a rental car, a phone with no island numbers in it, and a hotel that has told them the shelter is being arranged.

CARDS.name: Walter Finch
CARDS.text: Lives alone on Strand Road at the water's edge, has ridden out four hurricanes, will not leave without being asked in person by someone he knows.

CARDS.name: Sam Oyelaran
CARDS.text: Lives in Caldera village on the lake's south shore with his wife and a six-week-old daughter. When the Switchbacks slide he is at the dam and they are below the lower lane.

CARDS.name: Dolores Quint
CARDS.text: Twenty-nine years on the extraction floor, type 1 diabetic, insulin in the works' canteen fridge, which is on grid power.

CARDS.name: Mateo Iglesias
CARDS.text: Stays at the dam because his father is on the operator roster; nobody has told him he can go.

CARDS.name: The Gorge Road tanker crew
CARDS.text: Two Haven drivers who agree to bring diesel up to the dam's control generators if the road is still open when they are sent.

CARDS.name: Anh Tran
CARDS.text: Her two children are in Southfield Block C with her mother. She will finish the batch if asked and she will not ask to leave.

CARDS.name: Rubén Castillo
CARDS.text: Eleven years; has never signed a batch he could not stand behind. The custody log for batch 47 has a gap where the night tech evacuated.

CARDS.name: Gloria Adebayo-Ferris
CARDS.text: Lives on the ground floor of Southfield Block C, uses a wheelchair, looks after Anh Tran's children on shift nights. Block C is the lowest building on the flat.

CARDS.name: Kofi Mensah
CARDS.text: Knows every road and every creek crossing, and which ones go under first. If the trucks go to Southfield, he drives the first one.

CARDS.name: Dmitri Volkov
CARDS.text: Thirty years on the port; two months from retirement; the only operator certified on the big crane that loads the Kestrel Reach. Loading in the wind means Dmitri in the cab.

CARDS.name: Jonah Baptiste
CARDS.text: Lives with his grandmother in a ground-floor flat two streets from the terminal. Volunteers for everything. He is one of the two on the terminal night watch.

CARDS.name: Elena Marsh
CARDS.text: Single mother; her son is in the school shelter at Summit. She is the other half of the Tank 3 watch, and she is the one who reports the seal variance.

CARDS.name: The Sato family
CARDS.text: Run the dockside noodle bar that feeds the night shift, live above it at sea level, and will stay open as long as there are crews to feed.

CARDS.name: Dr. Amara Osei
CARDS.text: The island's only intensivist. Lives in Riverside, a ten-minute walk below the hospital, with a mother who does not walk well.

CARDS.name: Sgt. Ben Whitlock
CARDS.text: Runs the lower town's officers and two police boats. His wife is a nurse on the hospital's surgical floor. He will go into the water if sent, and if not sent.

CARDS.name: Ruth Calloway
CARDS.text: Her next session falls at T-6h. Lives alone on Hospital Hill, safe from the water, not from a power failure.

CARDS.name: Hannah Brecht's third grade
CARDS.text: Twenty-six pupils whose parents work shifts at Keystone and Haven; their teacher stays because nobody has come for them.

CARDS.name: Ji-woo Park
CARDS.text: The only person who can keep the satellite uplink aligned by hand when the automatic tracking fails, which it does above 90 mph. The dish is on the tower roof.

CARDS.name: Dr. Yusuf Haddad
CARDS.text: Four months out from a bone-marrow transplant, immunosuppressed, in executive housing on the headland with his wife. A crowded shelter is a danger to him that it is to no one else.

CARDS.name: Celeste Dubois
CARDS.line: 29, executive assistant to the Regional President
CARDS.text: Works on the 30th floor and lives in Riverside, across the bridge, because that is what an assistant's salary buys. She is at the campus gate with her neighbours at the peak.

CARDS.name: The Whitfield twins
CARDS.line: 9, children of the VP of Operations
CARDS.text: At home on the headland with a nanny while both parents are in the crisis room. Their names are on the first helicopter manifest.
